a11y.name: Accessibility
a11y.description: Make interfaces usable with a keyboard and a screen reader. Stripe, Vercel, OpenAI and Notion all list accessibility among the responsibilities.
a11y.practice: Go through a dropdown menu and a modal component using only the keyboard and VoiceOver, fix every issue, then re-check with axe.

a2a.name: Agent-to-Agent Protocols
a2a.description: Moonshot AI treats collaboration between agents as a new harness that needs a designed interaction protocol.
a2a.practice: Define a message format for handing a task from one agent to another, including the goal, a context summary and deliverables.

ab-test.name: A/B Testing & Experiments
ab-test.description: Use online experiments to verify how a change affects real users: traffic splitting, metrics, significance and guardrails. Good offline evals do not guarantee online impact.
concepts: Aligning offline evals with online metrics
ab-test.practice: Design an A/B experiment for two prompt versions: define primary and guardrail metrics, estimate the sample size, and write a results template.

abstraction.name: Platform Abstractions
abstraction.description: OpenAI asks for complex systems to be abstracted into simple, durable primitives.
abstraction.practice: Pick an existing agent framework and write a one-page critique of which abstractions will become obsolete as models get stronger.

agentic.name: Agentic Ways of Working
agentic.description: Baidu requires production-level, in-depth use of tools like Claude Code and Codex, and driving their adoption across the team.
agentic.practice: For one week, hand every coding task to a coding agent first and record the patterns of success and failure.

ai-ux.name: AI Product UX
ai-ux.description: Make uncertain model output trustworthy, controllable and easy to use: citations and sourcing, visible progress and reasoning, human confirmation and correction.
ai-ux.practice: Add citation markers, click-through to the source and a "wrong answer" feedback button to a RAG Q&A, and observe whether users trust the results more.

aiops.name: AI-Assisted Operations
aiops.description: Use LLMs and agents for alert summarization, log analysis, root cause inference and auto-remediation, with evaluation, permissions and human confirmation around them. Several 2026 SRE JDs added this requirement.
concepts: Diagnostic agents grounded in knowledge bases and runbooks
Permissions and human confirmation for auto-remediation
aiops.practice: Build a diagnostic assistant: given an alert, it pulls the related metrics and logs and outputs likely causes and suggested runbook steps; evaluate its hit rate on 10 past incidents.

api-design.name: API Design
api-design.description: The contract between services and between frontend and backend: resource modeling, protocol choice (REST / gRPC / GraphQL), version compatibility and error models. Once an API ships, it is hard to change.
concepts: Pagination, idempotency keys and error models
api-design.practice: Design both REST and gRPC APIs for an order service, and write the rules for version evolution and idempotency keys.

api-gateway.name: Gateways & Traffic Control
api-gateway.description: Tencent WeChat's access platform builds L7 gateways, Meituan hires for L7 traffic gateways and long-connection gateways, and NetEase owns routing, canary, rate limiting and circuit breaking in its traffic gateway. The gateway is the entry point for all traffic.
concepts: Auth, rate limiting and circuit breaking plugins
api-gateway.practice: Set up a gateway with Envoy or Nginx, configure header-based canary routing, token-bucket rate limiting and circuit breaking, and verify with a load test.

async.name: Async Execution
async.description: OpenAI's Agent Runtime emphasizes async execution and progress reporting; Anthropic Managed Agents must keep running after a session disconnects and recover cleanly.
async.practice: Run a 30-minute agent task in the background where the client can disconnect, reconnect and see live progress.

auth.name: Authentication (OAuth/OIDC)
auth.description: Authentication answers "who are you" and authorization answers "what can you do": sessions and tokens, OAuth2 / OIDC sign-in, and RBAC / ReBAC permission models.
auth.practice: Add OIDC sign-in to a multi-service app, then implement document-level permissions with a ReBAC model (such as OpenFGA).

autoscaling.name: Autoscaling
autoscaling.description: Pod-level and node-level autoscaling that keeps latency in check during traffic spikes and cuts cost during troughs.
autoscaling.practice: Configure HPA and Karpenter for a service, watch the Pod and node scale-out timeline under load testing, and find the slowest step.

backfill.name: Migrations & Backfills
backfill.description: Changing a model means backfilling history, and changing engines means migrating. Airbnb asks you to do this safely through dependency analysis, validation and controlled cutover.
concepts: Old-vs-new table reconciliation and dual runs
backfill.practice: Add a new column to a table with a year of data, design a backfill plan (batches, validation, cutover, rollback), and run a small-scale drill.

bi-dashboard.name: BI & Data Visualization
bi-dashboard.description: The last mile of data products: reports, dashboards and self-service analytics. Discord and Brex list Looker / Tableau as a plus.
bi-dashboard.practice: Build a dashboard with 5 core metrics on top of your own mart tables using Superset or Looker Studio.

biz-automation.name: Business Process Automation
biz-automation.description: Embed LLMs into a company's existing systems and processes, connect data and services, and automate end to end. PayPay asks for end-to-end business automation combining SaaS, AI and data platforms, Tencent WeCom connects companies' own data, and ByteDance Lark Base and Baidu build no-code/low-code AI app builders.
concepts: Integrating SaaS and internal system APIs
biz-automation.practice: Pick an expense or approval process, automate it end to end with an LLM and two internal APIs, and mark the steps that need human confirmation.

browser-render.name: Browser Rendering
browser-render.description: The pipeline from HTML to pixels. Baidu and Alibaba Qwen ask for familiarity with browser rendering, and Notion cares about how code affects rendering.
concepts: Main thread, compositor thread and GPU acceleration
Multi-process architecture and the renderer process
browser-render.practice: Record a janky scroll in the Performance panel, find the code that forces synchronous layout, and fix it.

build-tools.name: Build Tools & Bundling
build-tools.description: Build toolchains such as Webpack, Vite and Babel. Alibaba asks for mastery of Webpack/Vite/Babel, Ramp uses Vite, and Notion mentions bundlers and code splitting.
concepts: Module bundling and the dependency graph
build-tools.practice: Write a Webpack plugin and a Vite plugin, then analyze a project's bundle and cut its size by 30%.

cache.name: Caching
cache.description: Use caching to cut latency, absorb read traffic and reduce downstream load, while handling consistency, cache penetration, hot-key stampedes and mass expiry (avalanche). Redis is the most common implementation.
concepts: Redis data structures, persistence and clustering
cache.practice: Add a Redis cache to a read-heavy endpoint, simulate a hot key expiring, and prevent a cache stampede with a mutex or logical expiration.

capacity.name: Capacity Planning
capacity.description: Forecast demand, assess capacity headroom, and use single-node and full-chain load tests to verify that the system can handle peaks and big sales events.
concepts: Preparing for big sales events and peaks
capacity.practice: Run a step load test against a service with k6, find the inflection point, and estimate how many instances are needed to handle 3x traffic.

chaos.name: Chaos Engineering
chaos.description: Inject failures on purpose to test how the system and the team respond, and find weaknesses before real incidents do.
concepts: Fault injection tools (such as Chaos Mesh)
chaos.practice: Inject pod failures and network latency into a test cluster with Chaos Mesh, check whether the service holds its SLO, and write a drill report.

ci-cd.name: CI/CD
ci-cd.description: The automated pipeline from commit to production: build, test, artifacts, deploy and rollback, plus the speed and reliability of the pipeline itself.
ci-cd.practice: Build a full pipeline for a service with GitHub Actions or GitLab CI: test, build the image, push it to a registry, and deploy to staging.

ckpt.name: Checkpoint Recovery
ckpt.description: Alibaba requires checkpoint recovery to keep long-running tasks reliable; Xiaohongshu (RED) requires resume-from-checkpoint and failover.
ckpt.practice: Kill the process at an arbitrary step and verify the agent resumes from the checkpoint without repeating side effects.

cloud.name: Public Cloud (AWS/GCP)
cloud.description: The four basics of compute, networking, storage and identity/permissions, plus choosing managed services and architecture best practices. Most roles require production experience with AWS or GCP.
concepts: Compute options: VMs, containers, Serverless, managed K8s
cloud.practice: Deploy a three-tier app on AWS or GCP with a VPC, load balancer, container runtime, managed database and object storage; configure IAM with least privilege, draw the network topology and estimate the monthly cost.

cloud-dw.name: Cloud Data Warehouses
cloud-dw.description: Managed data warehouses such as Snowflake, BigQuery, Redshift and MaxCompute. Almost every US JD asks for at least one.
cloud-dw.practice: Within the BigQuery or Snowflake free tier, create a partitioned and clustered table, and compare the data scanned and cost of the same query before and after optimization.

cloud-governance.name: Cloud Account Governance
cloud-governance.description: Organization structure across many accounts and projects, least-privilege IAM and centralized controls. Platform roles in finance explicitly ask for managing dozens of AWS accounts.
cloud-governance.practice: Design a dev/staging/prod account structure with AWS Organizations or the GCP resource hierarchy, and write the SCPs or organization policies.

collab-editor.name: Rich Text & Collaboration
collab-editor.description: Documents, editors and real-time multi-user interfaces. OpenAI ChatGPT Space lists rich-text editors and real-time interfaces as a plus.
collab-editor.practice: Build a document two people can edit at the same time with Yjs and ProseMirror, and handle reconnecting after a disconnect.

conc.name: Concurrency & Quotas
conc.description: Model calls are rate limited, sandboxes have resource caps, and multi-tenancy requires fairness.
conc.practice: Implement a model-call proxy with per-tenant rate limiting.

concurrency.name: Concurrent Programming
concurrency.description: PayPay asks for a deep understanding of concurrency, Robinhood for designing high-concurrency systems, and Meituan for understanding multithreading. Threads, locks and memory models underpin backend correctness and performance.
concurrency.practice: Implement a bounded blocking queue and a fixed-size thread pool, and verify them with a race detector (Go -race or jcstress).

config-mgmt.name: Configuration Management
config-mgmt.description: Declarative configuration and consistency management for large server fleets; bare-metal and VM fleets still rely on it heavily.
concepts: Push vs. pull models in Ansible / Salt
config-mgmt.practice: Write an Ansible role that brings a batch of new machines to a common baseline (users, kernel parameters, monitoring agent), and rerun it to verify idempotency.

cost.name: Cost & Latency
cost.description: OpenAI expects measurable gains in task completion, cost and latency.
cost.practice: Measure a task's token distribution and halve its cost with caching and routing.

cpdp.name: Control & Data Plane
cpdp.description: Xiaohongshu (RED) explicitly requires being able to tell the two apart. A classic platform architecture idea.
cpdp.practice: Split your agent platform into a control plane and a data plane and draw the architecture diagram.

cpp.name: C++ Backend Development
cpp.description: Nearly every Tencent WeChat backend role requires strong C++, and Meituan's access gateway and Datadog list C/C++ too. High-performance backends and middleware are still largely written in C++.
cpp.practice: Write a thread-safe in-memory KV store in modern C++, and use ASan and perf to find leaks and hot spots.

cred.name: Credential Management
cred.description: Secrets must never enter the model's context.
concepts: Credential injection at the egress proxy
cred.practice: Implement a proxy that injects API keys at the network layer so code inside the sandbox never sees them.

cross-platform.name: H5, Mini Programs & RN
cross-platform.description: One tech stack across many platforms. Tencent and Baidu ask for mini program/hybrid development, Alibaba Yuchi asks for React Native or Flutter, and miive uses React Native (Expo).
cross-platform.practice: Build a small React Native (Expo) app that shares business logic with the web, and write a JSBridge that calls a native capability.

ctxeng.name: Context Engineering
ctxeng.description: Deciding what the model sees under a limited window and cost budget.
ctxeng.practice: Add automatic compaction to a long-running-task agent and compare success rates before and after.

cua.name: Computer / Browser Use
cua.description: A loop of screenshots, actions and observations, with VMs or browser environments as the underlying infrastructure.
cua.practice: Combine Playwright with a model to build a browser agent that can complete a form-filling task.

data-agent.name: Data Agents & NL2SQL
data-agent.description: Let agents find tables, write SQL and run analyses. Almost every Chinese JD is hiring for this: smart table discovery, natural-language data Q&A, smart ETL and quality inspection.
concepts: Metadata and semantic layers for agents
data-agent.practice: Build an NL2SQL prototype on a small data warehouse, evaluate its accuracy with 20 questions, and analyze whether errors come from finding tables or from writing SQL.

data-contracts.name: Data Contracts
data-contracts.description: Upstream produces the data and downstream consumes it, so both sides need to agree on schema, semantics and SLAs. Airbnb and Discord both ask for contracts defined at the source.
data-contracts.practice: Write a data contract for an upstream event (fields, types, constraints, SLA), and add a breaking-change check to CI.

data-cost.name: Data Cost Optimization
data-cost.description: Compute and storage bills grow linearly with data volume. Airbnb asks for lower compute costs, Tencent asks for lower data processing costs, and Meituan lists cost as a governance focus.
concepts: Compute resources and job cost attribution
Cost optimization for queries and jobs
data-cost.practice: Find the 10 most expensive jobs in a data warehouse over one week, optimize one of them, and quantify the compute saved.

data-fetch.name: Data Fetching
data-fetch.description: Loading, errors, retries, deduplication and caching for requests. Vercel asks you to handle validation, retries and duplicate requests, and OpenAI asks you to design UX for loading, errors and concurrent edits.
concepts: Request deduplication, cancellation and race conditions
data-fetch.practice: Build list editing with optimistic updates and rollback on failure using TanStack Query, and handle request races when switching quickly.

data-flywheel.name: Feedback & Error Analysis
data-flywheel.description: Keep improving from production failures: collect feedback, categorize bad cases, add them to the eval set, and run regressions after fixes. LayerX asks for analyzing failure cases and edge cases to improve the product, and Perplexity for continuous monitoring and iteration.
concepts: Error categorization and root cause analysis
Feeding bad cases back into eval sets
data-flywheel.practice: Pull 100 production conversation logs, categorize the failure reasons by hand, build an error distribution table, and add the top three categories to the eval set.

data-governance.name: Data Governance & Access
data-governance.description: Data standards, permissions, sensitive data and compliance. Coinbase asks for access control across storage layers, and PayPay asks for governance and security controls that meet compliance requirements.
data-governance.practice: Design row- and column-level permissions and a masking policy for a dataset, and implement part of it with Unity Catalog or Ranger.

data-integration.name: Data Integration
data-integration.description: Bring business databases, third-party APIs, SaaS and event streams into the data warehouse. Airbnb asks you to manage schema changes across many sources, and PayPay mentions CDC.
data-integration.practice: Sync changes from a MySQL table to Kafka with Debezium, then land them as a queryable snapshot table.

data-modeling.name: Data Modeling
data-modeling.description: Abstract business objects, events and relationships into data structures that can evolve over time. Models are hard to change once they ship, and transactional and analytical databases call for different trade-offs.
concepts: Primary keys, constraints and soft deletes
data-modeling.practice: Draw a conceptual model and a 3NF logical model for a food delivery business, then explain which tables should be denormalized for analytics.

data-observability.name: Data Observability & SLA
data-observability.description: Monitor the data itself: freshness, volume, distribution anomalies and SLAs. Discord asks for automated anomaly detection and SLA infrastructure.
data-observability.practice: Set up freshness and row-count monitoring for three core tables, detect anomalies with simple statistics, and hook them up to alerts.

data-platform.name: Self-Service Data Platform
data-platform.description: Turn pipelines, ingestion, quality and permissions into SDKs and self-service tools, so thousands of pipelines don't need to understand the internals. Coinbase has an entire role doing just this.
concepts: Paved paths and capturing best practices
data-platform.practice: Build a config-driven ingestion framework where one YAML file generates a three-step pipeline: extract, validate and load into the warehouse.

data-quality.name: Data Quality & Testing
data-quality.description: Accurate, complete, consistent and timely. Every JD asks for it: Airbnb asks for automated tests and reconciliation, and Discord asks for a quality framework for ML inputs.
concepts: Quality dimensions: completeness, accuracy, consistency, timeliness
Assertion-based data tests (dbt tests, Great Expectations)
data-quality.practice: Add 5 data tests to a pipeline (unique, not null, value range, referential integrity, row-count fluctuation), and block downstream jobs when they fail.

db-scaling.name: Database Scaling
db-scaling.description: The path once a single database can't keep up: replication, sharding and distributed SQL. PayPay's stack includes TiDB, NetEase asks for distributed database knowledge, Coinbase for distributed data storage experience, and Tencent works on HTAP queries.
concepts: Where OLTP ends and HTAP/OLAP begins
db-scaling.practice: Shard an orders table by user with Vitess or ShardingSphere, and handle cross-shard queries and globally unique IDs.

ddd.name: Domain Modeling
ddd.description: Meituan asks for abstracting complex business into clear domain models, and Money Forward for abstracting and modeling business domains. The extensibility of complex business systems comes from the model, not the amount of code.
ddd.practice: Draw a bounded context map for food delivery fulfillment (couriers, stations, delivery orders), and implement a dispatch use case with aggregates.

design-collab.name: Design to Code
design-collab.description: Work with designers to turn prototypes into products. OpenAI asks you to turn prototypes into production-quality work, Ramp asks for design-to-code, and Mirai Translate asks you to start development from UI/UX design.
concepts: Reading Figma: spacing, grids and variables
design-collab.practice: Take a Figma Community design, rebuild one page pixel-perfect, and list 5 decisions you would need to align on with the designer.

design-system.name: Design Systems
design-system.description: Reusable components, design tokens and theming. Stripe's Sail and Ramp's Ryu are both design system teams, and Chinese JDs commonly ask you to build up a component library.
design-system.practice: Build Button, Input and Dialog from scratch: token-driven theming, dark mode support, accessible, with docs published via Storybook.

devtools-debug.name: Browser Debugging
devtools-debug.description: Find problems with DevTools and evidence. Notion asks you to investigate bottlenecks with browser tools, Amap asks for fluency with Chrome DevTools, and PayPay asks you to triage and debug production issues.
concepts: DevTools breakpoints and the Network panel
Source maps and reproducing production bugs
devtools-debug.practice: Take a real error from Sentry, map it back with source maps, reproduce it locally, and write the fix plus a regression test.

devx.name: Developer Experience
devx.description: OpenAI emphasizes empathy for developers and working with research and product teams.
concepts: Turning research progress into platform capabilities
devx.practice: Have 3 colleagues try your platform and record where they get stuck.

dim-modeling.name: Dimensional Modeling
dim-modeling.description: The Kimball method: fact tables, dimension tables and slowly changing dimensions. Airbnb, Discord, Tencent and Meituan all list it as a hard requirement.
concepts: Fact table types (transaction, periodic snapshot, accumulating snapshot)
Conformed dimensions and the bus matrix
dim-modeling.practice: Design a star schema for a subscription business: an order fact table plus user and product dimensions, using SCD2 to record user tier changes.

dist.name: Distributed Systems
dist.description: Long-running tasks, state recovery and scheduling are distributed-systems problems at heart. All four companies list it as core.
concepts: Idempotency and the limits of exactly-once
dist.practice: Revisit the Raft lab from MIT 6.5840, focusing on idempotency and retry design.

dist-txn.name: Distributed Transactions
dist-txn.description: How to make writes across services and databases neither lost nor duplicated: idempotency, compensation and eventual consistency. The core problem in payment, order and inventory systems.
dist-txn.practice: Implement a cross-account transfer as a saga, inject a failure at every step, and prove that the final balances are conserved.

doc-parsing.name: Doc Parsing & Chunking
doc-parsing.description: Knowledge base quality depends on what happens before ingestion: PDFs, Office files and spreadsheets must be parsed and chunked first. LayerX's agents have to read receipts and invoices on their own, and ByteDance Douyin asks for organizing business information into a knowledge base.
doc-parsing.practice: Parse and ingest a batch of PDFs that contain tables, and compare the retrieval hit rate of three chunking strategies on 20 questions.

docker.name: Containers & Images
docker.description: Package an app and its runtime into an image so local, CI and production stay consistent. The smallest unit of cloud-native deployment.
docker.practice: Shrink a service image from 1GB to under 100MB, run it as non-root with a health check, then use compose to start the database and cache it depends on.

dr.name: Disaster Recovery
dr.description: Keep the business running or recover quickly during zone- or region-level failures: backup and restore, primary-standby failover, and cell-based active-active.
dr.practice: Design a cross-AZ disaster recovery plan for a service with a database, write the failover steps, run an actual restore drill, and record the RTO.

dsa.name: Data Structures & Algorithms
dsa.description: Hashing, trees, heaps, graphs and complexity analysis. Indexes, cache eviction, rate limiting and scheduling are all built on classic structures, and they are a standard part of interviews everywhere.
concepts: Hash tables, skip lists and B+ trees
Tree and graph traversal, topological sort
Sorting, binary search and two pointers
dsa.practice: Hand-write an LRU cache with TTL and a skip-list-based sorted set, and benchmark them against the standard library.

durable.name: Durable Execution
durable.description: The core of long-running tasks: processes will crash, but task state and results must not be lost.
durable.practice: Use Temporal to rewrite an agent loop as a recoverable workflow.

dw-layering.name: Warehouse Layers & Domains
dw-layering.description: ODS / DWD / DWS / ADS layering and subject areas are the common language of data warehouse roles in China. A Tencent e-commerce JD lists all five layers outright.
concepts: Responsibilities of the ODS / DWD / DWM / DWS / ADS layers
dw-layering.practice: Plan 20 source tables of an e-commerce business into a layered data warehouse, and write out the table list for each layer and a dependency graph.

electron.name: Electron Desktop Apps
electron.description: Build desktop apps with web technology. OpenAI's Codex App asks for an Electron-grade desktop experience, and Tencent asks for familiarity with main-renderer process communication.
electron.practice: Build a small Electron tool: expose file read/write over IPC safely, package it as macOS and Windows installers, and support auto-update.

embedding-search.name: Embeddings & Vector Search
embedding-search.description: Turning text into vectors for semantic retrieval is the foundation of RAG, recommendations and semantic search.
embedding-search.practice: Index 10,000 documents with pgvector and compare recall and latency of exact search vs. HNSW.

etl-elt.name: ETL / ELT Pipelines
etl-elt.description: The core work of turning source data into trusted datasets: extract, transform and load, plus incremental loads, idempotency and reruns.
concepts: Full loads, incremental loads and partition overwrite
etl-elt.practice: Implement an incremental ETL partitioned by day that can rerun any single day without producing duplicate data.

evals.name: Evals
evals.description: Turning a non-deterministic system into one that can be measured and compared.
evals.practice: Build 50 eval cases for your agent and establish a baseline score.

fe-arch.name: Frontend Architecture
fe-arch.description: Break a complex product into clear layers and module boundaries. Tencent WorkBuddy asks for frontend domain modeling and layering, and OpenAI asks you to own architectural decisions such as component systems and navigation.
concepts: Layers, module boundaries and dependency direction
fe-arch.practice: Draw the module dependency graph of a mid-sized SPA, add a lint rule that forbids cross-layer imports, and refactor out a standalone domain module.

fe-state.name: Frontend State Management
fe-state.description: Separating and syncing UI state, server state and URL state. OpenAI asks you to own the state management architecture, and Baidu asks for mastery of one of Redux/Mobx/Zustand.
fe-state.practice: Refactor an admin page that relies on prop drilling to Zustand plus URL state, and compare the number of re-renders.

fine-tune.name: Fine-Tuning & Alignment
fine-tune.description: When prompting and RAG are not enough, fine-tune a model on domain data. Ramp and Linear mention fine-tuning, ByteDance Douyin asks for LoRA/QLoRA and DPO, and Tencent WeChat mentions model fine-tuning. Application engineers need to judge when fine-tuning is worth it and how to prepare the data.
fine-tune.practice: Fine-tune a small open-source model with LoRA on a classification task, and compare quality and cost against a few-shot prompt.

finops.name: Cloud Cost (FinOps)
finops.description: Make cloud spend visible, attributable and optimizable: tagging and allocation, right-sizing, spot instances and commitment discounts.
finops.practice: Deploy OpenCost on a K8s cluster, produce a per-namespace cost report, and find the 3 biggest sources of waste.

gate.name: Regression Gates
gate.description: Every change to models, prompts and tools must be evaluated, compared and released safely.
gate.practice: Add an eval gate to CI that blocks merges when the score drops past a threshold.

gateway.name: LLM Gateway & Routing
gateway.description: Nearly all Japanese companies require an LLM gateway for centralized model switching, permissions and budgets. Cursor's Auto picks a model automatically based on need, capability and cost.
gateway.practice: Implement a gateway that routes to different models by task difficulty and budget, with fallback on failure.

gen-ui.name: Generative & Agentic UI
gen-ui.description: Interfaces generated dynamically from model output: cards, forms and artifact previews. ByteDance Lark is exploring Generative UI / Agentic UI, and Ramp lets agents produce interactive analyses on top of its data layer.
gen-ui.practice: Have the model return three component types via tool calls (weather card, table, chart), render them by type on the frontend, and send user edits back to the model.

git-collab.name: Git & Collaboration
git-collab.description: Branches, commits, pull requests and code review. Application code, infrastructure code and SQL models all follow the same collaboration workflow.
git-collab.practice: Open a PR on an open-source project, see it through review and revisions, then use git bisect to locate a regression.

gitops.name: GitOps
gitops.description: Git is the single source of truth, and controllers continuously reconcile the cluster to the declared state.
concepts: PR workflows for IaC such as Atlantis
gitops.practice: Manage the same app across two environments with Argo CD, promote versions through PRs, and demonstrate a rollback.

guard.name: Guardrails & Compliance
guard.description: JDs from Japanese companies commonly require personal data policies, usage restrictions and auditing; Cursor lists guardrails as part of the harness.
guard.practice: Design a guardrail layer for an internal agent: PII masking, blocking dangerous actions and an audit trail.

hadoop-hive.name: Hadoop & Hive
hadoop-hive.description: HDFS, YARN and Hive are still the foundation of offline data warehouses in China. Understanding MapReduce is the starting point for understanding later engines.
hadoop-hive.practice: Run a single-node Hadoop + Hive in Docker, create a partitioned table, and compare the data scanned with and without partition pruning.

harness.name: Harness Engineering
harness.description: Everything outside the model: context assembly, tools, the loop, approvals and telemetry. Xiaohongshu (RED) calls it the Harness Kernel; Baidu calls it harness engineering.
harness.practice: Read the open-source code of Codex CLI or OpenCode and draw its module diagram.

hitl.name: Human-in-the-Loop Design
hitl.description: Arent asks for a clear boundary between decisions humans confirm and decisions left to the agent; Moonshot AI is defining product forms for human-agent collaboration.
hitl.practice: Break a business process into steps and mark which ones need human approval based on risk and reversibility.

html-css.name: HTML & CSS
html-css.description: Semantic HTML and solid CSS are the foundation of every interface. Tencent asks for mastery of HTML5/CSS3, and Alibaba Chengyun asks for solid CSS fundamentals and handling of browser compatibility.
concepts: CSS variables, cascade layers and container queries
html-css.practice: Rebuild a complex admin page (sidebar, table, modal) with HTML/CSS only, without a single line of JS, and make it match in three browsers.

http-cache.name: Browser & CDN Caching
http-cache.description: HTTP caching, CDNs and Service Workers. Vercel asks for an understanding of server rendering and caching, Notion mentions service workers and asset caching, and PayPay lists CDN as a plus.
http-cache.practice: Design a caching strategy for an SPA: no caching for HTML, long-lived caching for static assets, then add a Service Worker for offline access.

hybrid.name: Hybrid & Self-Hosted
hybrid.description: Anthropic Managed Agents run both in hosted sandboxes and in customer-owned environments; Xiaohongshu (RED) wants unified management of Managed and BYO agents.
concepts: One control plane, many data planes
hybrid.practice: Design an environment interface so the same agent can run in your sandbox or in a customer VPC.

i18n.name: Internationalization
i18n.description: Copy, formatting and layout for multiple languages and regions. Stripe asks for improving the design system's internationalization, and PayPay's stack includes i18n.
concepts: String extraction and ICU message format
i18n.practice: Integrate FormatJS into an app, support Chinese, Japanese and English plus currency formatting, and load language packs on demand.

iac.name: Infrastructure as Code
iac.description: Declare and change infrastructure in code, and make changes reviewable, reversible and checked for drift.
iac.practice: Write a reusable Terraform module (VPC + cluster) and deploy two environments through a PR + plan review process.

identity.name: Agent Identity & Auth
identity.description: On whose behalf is the agent acting? It needs identity, delegated authorization and least privilege.
identity.practice: Design the authorization flow for an agent accessing GitHub on a user's behalf, with revocable and auditable permissions.

idp.name: Internal Developer Platform
idp.description: Package infrastructure as self-service tools and golden paths so product engineers can stand up a new service in minutes. The core output of platform engineering.
idp.practice: Build a 'New Service' wizard with Backstage software templates that generates the repo, CI, deployment config and alerts in one go.

incident.name: Incident Response
incident.description: Command, communication and mitigation during major incidents, followed by blameless postmortems and tracking of action items.
concepts: Blameless postmortems and closing action items
incident.practice: Pick a public incident report from a large tech company and rewrite it with a postmortem template: timeline, impact, root cause, what went well and action items.

infra-security.name: Infra Security & Compliance
infra-security.description: Secret management, policy as code, cluster hardening and compliance auditing, so the platform is secure by default.
infra-security.practice: Deploy Kyverno on a K8s cluster, write 3 policies (block privileged, require resource limits, allow only the internal image registry), and verify they block violations.

inject.name: Prompt Injection & Tools
inject.description: Indirect injection and data exfiltration are the most realistic security risks for agents in production.
concepts: The combined risk of private data, untrusted content and external communication
inject.practice: Red-team your own agent: use web page content to trick it into leaking data.

iso.name: Isolation Technologies
iso.description: Mentioned by all four companies. The security and performance trade-offs among containers, gVisor, Firecracker and Kata are a frequent interview topic.
iso.practice: On the same machine, compare startup latency and syscall overhead across three runtimes.

js-core.name: JavaScript Fundamentals
js-core.description: Closures, prototypes, async code and the event loop. Ramp lists a deep understanding of JavaScript first, and almost every Chinese JD requires fluency in ES6+.
js-core.practice: Implement Promise.all, debounce, throttle and a minimal event emitter by hand, and cover the edge cases with tests.

jvm.name: Java & the JVM
jvm.description: Java / Kotlin services and big data engines such as Spark, Flink and Hive all run on the JVM. Understanding the memory model, GC and diagnostic tools is a prerequisite for tuning and troubleshooting.
concepts: JVM memory areas and class loading
JVM languages such as Kotlin / Scala
Diagnostic tools such as Arthas and JFR
jvm.practice: Introduce a memory leak and full GCs into a Spring Boot service, then locate and fix them with JFR and MAT.

k8s.name: Cloud Native & K8s
k8s.description: Baidu explicitly requires Operator experience, and Alibaba requires K8s/Serverless. Most sandbox instance orchestration is built on K8s.
k8s.practice: Write an Operator with kubebuilder that manages a Sandbox CRD.

k8s-cluster-ops.name: K8s Cluster Operations
k8s-cluster-ops.description: Upgrades, node pool strategy, add-on management, etcd operations and troubleshooting for production clusters. Everyday work for platform teams.
concepts: Zero-downtime control plane and node upgrades
k8s-cluster-ops.practice: Build a multi-node cluster with kind or kubeadm, perform a minor version upgrade, and keep a service available throughout.

k8s-controller.name: K8s Controllers & Operators
k8s-controller.description: Write custom controllers, CRDs and admission webhooks with controller-runtime, turning operational knowledge into reconcile loops.
k8s-controller.practice: Write an Operator with kubebuilder: declaring one CR automatically creates a Deployment, a Service and alerting rules. Cover it with envtest tests.

k8s-net.name: K8s Networking
k8s-net.description: How Pod networking, Services, Ingress and network policies are implemented, and how to debug failures that cross network boundaries.
concepts: Services and the kube-proxy / eBPF data plane
k8s-net.practice: Capture packets in a cluster to trace a Pod-to-Service request and explain the NAT and routing at every hop. Then add a NetworkPolicy and verify the isolation.

lakehouse.name: Lakehouse & Table Formats
lakehouse.description: Iceberg, Hudi and Delta bring transactions and schema evolution to data on object storage. Airbnb, Tencent, Alibaba and PayPay all use lakehouses.
concepts: Snapshots and transactions in Iceberg / Hudi / Delta
lakehouse.practice: Create an Iceberg table with Spark, make a schema change and run a time-travel query, then compact the small files.

lang.name: Go / Rust / Python
lang.description: Go for the platform and control plane, Rust for sandboxes and high-performance components, Python for the agent and evals ecosystem.
lang.practice: Implement a tool executor in Go that propagates cancellation and timeouts.

ledger.name: Ledger & Fund Correctness
ledger.description: Stripe handles billions of money movement requests, Coinbase detects money-flow invariants in real time instead of quarterly reconciliation, PayPay is rebuilding its core banking system, and Tencent runs WeChat Pay. A capability specific to financial backends.
ledger.practice: Implement a double-entry ledger service that supports transfers, reversals and end-of-day reconciliation, and use randomized tests to verify that debits and credits always balance.

lifecycle.name: Agent Assets & Lifecycle
lifecycle.description: A unified model for agent artifacts, owners, versions, permissions, policies and releases.
lifecycle.practice: Design a schema for an agent artifact that covers identity, versions and policies.

lint-quality.name: Linting & Static Analysis
lint-quality.description: Linting, formatting and large-scale code changes. Stripe mentions codemods and lint rules, and Baidu asks for mastery of toolchain tools such as ESLint.
lint-quality.practice: Write a custom ESLint rule, then write a codemod with jscodeshift to migrate a deprecated API across the codebase.

linux-shell.name: Linux & Shell
linux-shell.description: Big data jobs run on Linux clusters, and debugging jobs, reading logs and writing ops scripts all depend on the shell.
linux-shell.practice: Write a shell script that counts errors in the logs under a directory and aggregates them by hour, then schedule it with cron.

llm.name: LLM Fundamentals
llm.description: Building an agent platform requires understanding the model's input and output constraints.
llm.practice: Without a framework, call the API directly to implement a multi-turn tool-calling exchange.

llm-api.name: LLM API Integration
llm-api.description: The basics of wiring a model into a product: auth, streaming, retries, timeouts and multi-turn message assembly. Ubie requires building and operating systems on LLM APIs, and Notion and Ramp require using LLMs in real production scenarios.
llm-api.practice: Wrap a unified model client that supports two vendors, streaming output and exponential backoff retries, and logs tokens and latency for every call.

llm-workflow.name: LLM Workflow Orchestration
llm-workflow.description: Chain multiple model calls, retrieval steps and tools into reliable business processes. ByteDance Lark Base asks for workflow orchestration, Tencent for production experience with LangChain / dify, and Linear wants to turn models into structured, reliable workflows.
llm-workflow.practice: Implement a "retrieve -> draft -> self-check -> revise" workflow in LangGraph that can be rerun after a failure at any step.

log-pipeline.name: Log Pipelines
log-pipeline.description: Collecting, parsing, storing and searching logs at scale, and keeping the cost under control. Both troubleshooting and auditing depend on it.
log-pipeline.practice: Ship K8s container logs to Loki with Fluent Bit, and query all logs for a single request by trace_id in Grafana.

loop.name: Agent Loop
loop.description: The loop of model, tools and observations: the minimal kernel of every agent.
concepts: Returning tool errors to the model
loop.practice: Implement a complete agent loop in under 200 lines, with approvals and interrupts.

mcp.name: MCP
mcp.description: The de facto standard protocol for connecting tools and data.
mcp.practice: Write an MCP server for an internal system you know well and connect it to Claude or Codex.

memory.name: Layered Memory
memory.description: Short-term, working and long-term memory, plus write and retrieval strategies.
concepts: When to write and handling conflicts
memory.practice: Implement a file-based memory tool for an agent and test cross-session recall.

metadata-lineage.name: Metadata & Lineage
metadata-lineage.description: Help people and agents find tables, understand columns and trace upstream and downstream. Coinbase, Alibaba and Tencent all mention lineage and catalogs.
metadata-lineage.practice: Collect the lineage of an Airflow pipeline with OpenLineage or DataHub, and trace a column's upstream in the UI.

metrics-layer.name: Metrics & Semantic Layer
metrics-layer.description: Unify metric definitions so that reports, experiments and AI queries all use the same definitions. Airbnb uses Minerva, Discord maintains a semantic layer, and Tencent and Meituan ask for consistent definitions.
metrics-layer.practice: Define 5 core metrics for a subscription product (with definitions, dimensions and SQL), and implement two of them with the dbt semantic layer.

metrics-monitoring.name: Metrics & Time Series
metrics-monitoring.description: Metrics systems typified by Prometheus: collection, storage, querying and visualization, plus the engineering problems of high cardinality and long-term storage.
concepts: High cardinality and long-term storage (Thanos / Mimir)
metrics-monitoring.practice: Deploy Prometheus + Grafana on a local K8s cluster, add RED metrics to a service, and write 3 PromQL-based alerting rules.

micro-fe.name: Micro-Frontends
micro-fe.description: A way to split large apps where multiple teams and tech stacks coexist. PayPay's stack includes single-spa, and both Baidu and Alibaba list micro-frontend experience as a plus.
micro-fe.practice: Mount a Vue sub-app and a React sub-app into the same host app with single-spa or qiankun.

microservices.name: Microservices & Governance
microservices.description: Coinbase, PayPay, Money Forward and NetEase all ask for microservices experience, and Meituan calls it SOA. Service boundaries, service discovery, RPC and governance are everyday work.
concepts: Service registry, discovery and RPC frameworks
microservices.practice: Split a monolith into three services, add a service registry and distributed tracing, and record how latency and failure surface change before and after.

ml-data.name: Feature & Training Data
ml-data.description: Feed models: features, labels, samples and training data quality. Discord Ads asks for feature and label generation, and Fliggy asks for real-time/offline user features.
ml-data.practice: Define a set of user features with Feast, export an offline training set and read them online, and verify the two sides match.

mobile-llm.name: Mobile & On-Device LLMs
mobile-llm.description: Integrating models into apps: streaming, sessions, poor networks and on-device inference. Tencent Hunyuan hires for iOS/Android LLM app development, including running quantized models on-device and optimizing time to first token.
mobile-llm.practice: Run a small quantized model on a phone for offline summarization, switch to a cloud model when online, and compare time to first token and battery drain.

motion.name: Motion & Interaction
motion.description: The details that make a UI feel right: layout, motion and typography. OpenAI asks you to polish motion and interaction details, and Ramp lists GSAP and Motion as a plus.
motion.practice: Add add, remove and reorder animations (FLIP) to a list, keep it at 60fps, and respect the reduced-motion setting.

mq.name: Messaging & Streams
mq.description: Message queues provide async decoupling, peak shaving and event-driven design; log-based systems like Kafka are also the entry point for real-time data pipelines. The core is partitions, consumer groups and delivery semantics.
concepts: Event-driven design and the Outbox pattern
mq.practice: Set up a Kafka order-event stream, deliberately restart consumers and reprocess messages, and use an idempotency table to keep results correct.

multi.name: Multi-Agent Delegation
multi.description: Subagents, delegation and parallel execution. The hard parts are context isolation and merging results.
multi.practice: Implement a research task where a lead agent dispatches 3 subagents in parallel.

multimodal.name: Multimodal Applications
multimodal.description: Mixed input and output across images, speech and documents. Tencent WeChat asks for multimodal interaction pipelines, ByteDance Lark for rendering multimodal messages, and Tencent Hunyuan covers voice input and text-to-speech playback.
multimodal.practice: Build a screenshot Q&A feature: the user uploads a screenshot and asks a question, and the model answers with descriptions of the relevant regions.

net.name: Computer Networking
net.description: Agent platforms rely heavily on streaming and long-lived connections, and egress control is also a security boundary.
net.practice: Write an LLM gateway that forwards SSE streams, with timeouts and retries.

net-programming.name: Network Programming & I/O
net-programming.description: Tencent asks for Linux network programming, and NetEase for deep knowledge of Netty/Reactor and long-lived SSE connections. The I/O model sets the throughput ceiling of high-concurrency services and gateways.
concepts: The Reactor pattern and event loops
TCP message framing, backpressure and connection management
net-programming.practice: Write an echo/push server with epoll or Netty that handles tens of thousands of long-lived connections, load test it, and watch the CPU and connection-count curves.

node-bff.name: Node.js & BFF
node-bff.description: Server-side skills for frontend engineers. Alibaba asks for Node.js with express/koa experience, PayPay uses NestJS and Express, and Vercel asks you to write server-side code.
node-bff.practice: Write a BFF in NestJS that aggregates two backend APIs, with timeouts, retries and structured logging.

nosql.name: NoSQL & KV Stores
nosql.description: KV, wide-column and document stores model data around access patterns rather than normal forms, gaining horizontal scale and high availability at the cost of consistency and query flexibility.
nosql.practice: Model an access-log table in both DynamoDB and Cassandra, and compare how partition key choice affects hot spots.

observability.name: Monitoring, Logs & Alerts
observability.description: Designing metrics, logs and traces as a whole, so you find problems before users do and can quickly answer "what broke and why".
concepts: Four golden signals and the RED / USE methods
Symptom-based alerting and alert noise reduction
observability.practice: Instrument a service with OpenTelemetry, build a RED dashboard in Grafana, and write three alerts that fire only when a human needs to act.

olap.name: OLAP Engines
olap.description: MPP engines for ad hoc queries and reports. Chinese JDs often name Doris, ClickHouse and StarRocks, and Chime asks for experience with MPP databases.
olap.practice: Load tens of millions of rows into Doris or ClickHouse and compare query times under different partitioning, bucketing and materialized view setups.

oncall.name: On-Call & Runbooks
oncall.description: Sustainable on-call: alerts fire only when a human needs to act, every alert has a runbook, and on-call load is measurable and trending down.
oncall.practice: Audit all alerts for a service, delete or merge the non-actionable ones, and write a runbook for each one that remains.

oop-design.name: OOP & Design Patterns
oop-design.description: Meituan and NetEase ask for familiarity with design patterns, and PayPay for OOP fundamentals. Maintainable business code depends on clear abstractions and separation of responsibilities.
concepts: Common creational, structural and behavioral patterns
Dependency injection and inversion of control
oop-design.practice: Take a piece of business code full of if-else chains, refactor it with the strategy pattern and dependency injection, and add unit tests.

orchestration.name: Workflow Orchestration
orchestration.description: Manage dependencies, retries and SLAs for hundreds or thousands of tasks with DAGs. Airflow is the most common, Discord uses Dagster, and Chinese companies mostly use in-house schedulers.
orchestration.practice: Orchestrate a three-step pipeline (extract, transform, validate) with Airflow or Dagster, with retries on failure and SLA alerts.

os.name: Linux & OS
os.description: Namespaces, cgroups, seccomp, file systems and the process model. The foundation of every isolation technology and sandbox.
os.practice: Build a minimal container by hand with unshare and cgroups, limiting CPU, memory and network.

otel-tracing.name: Distributed Tracing (OTel)
otel-tracing.description: Propagate context across microservices to reconstruct the full call chain of a request and pinpoint where it is slow or failing.
otel-tracing.practice: Instrument two services that call each other with OpenTelemetry, send the data through the Collector to Jaeger or Tempo, create a slow call and locate it with a trace.

patterns.name: Execution Patterns
patterns.description: Xiaohongshu (RED) requires support for different execution architectures such as ReAct, Workflow, Planner-Executor and Multi-Agent.
patterns.practice: Implement the same task both as a workflow and as an autonomous agent, and compare success rate and cost.

perf.name: Performance Optimization
perf.description: Measure, locate, optimize, then guard against regressions: find bottlenecks across CPU, memory, I/O, network and runtime, and quantify the gains.
concepts: Runtime tuning (GC, thread pools, connection pools)
perf.practice: Load test an HTTP service, generate flame graphs with perf / pprof, find and optimize the hottest path, and compare P99 before and after.

pkg-monorepo.name: Package Mgmt & Monorepos
pkg-monorepo.description: Dependencies, versions and multi-package repos. Stripe lists package managers and large monorepos as a plus, and Alibaba Qwen mentions pnpm.
pkg-monorepo.practice: Set up a monorepo with a component library, a utility library and an app using pnpm workspaces and Turborepo, with incremental builds.

product-sense.name: AI Product Sense
product-sense.description: Judge which problems suit AI and how good is good enough. Linear asks for product sense, Figma for connecting modeling work to business value, LayerX for discovering and defining problems in customers' businesses, and Tencent for strong product awareness.
concepts: Matching user problems to AI capabilities
Working with product, design and ML teams
product-sense.practice: Pick an existing product feature and write a one-page "should we add AI" analysis: user problem, cost of failure, success metrics and a minimum viable approach.

prompt-eng.name: Prompt Engineering
prompt-eng.description: Use instructions, examples and structure to get consistent, intended output from a model, and version and evaluate prompts the way you would code.
prompt-eng.practice: Write three prompt versions for a customer-support reply scenario, compare them on 30 fixed test cases, and record each version's changes and score.

proto.name: Rapid Prototyping (0 to 1)
proto.description: AI features are highly uncertain, so validate with a prototype before investing. Figma asks for 0-to-1 prototyping experience, Linear for prototyping and iterating on intelligent workflows, Notion for taking prototypes to shipped features, and PayPay for moving from PoC to full development.
concepts: Knowing when to stop and walk away
proto.practice: Build an AI feature prototype in two days, validate it on 10 real user cases, and list what must be added before it goes to production.

python.name: Python Engineering
python.description: The main language of AI applications and data engineering: model SDKs, data pipelines, scheduling DAGs and eval scripts usually ship a Python version first.
concepts: Type hints and project layout (pyproject, uv)
Pydantic validation and testable module design
python.practice: Write a Python CLI that reads CSV, cleans it and writes Parquet, with unit tests and type checking.

query-opt.name: Query Optimization
query-opt.description: At massive scale, a SQL query that is an order of magnitude slower means missed SLAs and doubled costs. Tencent, Meituan and Alibaba all ask for large-scale SQL tuning experience.
query-opt.practice: Pick a slow query, read its execution plan to find the bottleneck, and halve the run time by rewriting it or changing the join strategy.

rag.name: Retrieval & RAG
rag.description: OpenAI mentions search and connected context; Alibaba mentions knowledge retrieval.
rag.practice: On the same corpus, compare hybrid retrieval with an agent searching on its own via grep.

react.name: React
react.description: The most common frontend framework, mentioned by 10 companies. Baidu asks for an understanding of the virtual DOM, diffing and Fiber.
react.practice: Without reading the source, write a mini React (createElement, render, useState), then compare it with Fiber scheduling in the React source.

realtime-dw.name: Real-Time Data Warehouse
realtime-dw.description: Move the layered data warehouse onto a real-time pipeline: real-time detail, real-time aggregates and live dashboards. Tencent e-commerce asks for a real-time data warehouse built on Flink SQL.
concepts: Real-time layering and dimension table joins
Unified batch and streaming and data lakes (Paimon / Hudi)
realtime-dw.practice: Build a Kafka to Flink SQL to Doris real-time pipeline, produce a live GMV dashboard, and reconcile it with offline results.

registry.name: Tool Registry & Gateway
registry.description: Registration, versioning, discovery and call governance for tools, Skills and MCP servers.
registry.practice: Design an MCP gateway that unifies auth, rate limiting and auditing across multiple MCP servers.

render-perf.name: Runtime Perf & Memory
render-perf.description: Smooth interactions without jank or leaks. Tencent WorkBuddy asks you to optimize frame rate and memory usage and track down memory leaks, and OpenAI asks for rendering performance.
render-perf.practice: Build a virtualized list with 100,000 rows, then use React Profiler and heap snapshots to find and fix a re-render storm and a leak.

research.name: Research Taste
research.description: Xiaohongshu (RED) asks for testable hypotheses and judging approaches with experiments and benchmarks.
concepts: Publishing as open source or articles
research.practice: Each week, read one agent systems paper closely and write a short verdict on whether it is reproducible and worth pursuing.

resilience.name: Resilience Patterns
resilience.description: Keep a system partially available under overload and dependency failures instead of letting it cascade into collapse.
concepts: Rate limiting algorithms (token bucket, sliding window)
resilience.practice: Add timeouts, jittered retries, circuit breaking and rate limiting to a service that calls a downstream, and use fault injection to show that a slow downstream does not take down the upstream.

responsive.name: Responsive & Multi-Device
responsive.description: One interface that works on desktop, mobile and mini programs. Stripe and Ramp ask for responsive design, and Tencent asks for cross-device consistency and mobile adaptation.
responsive.practice: Turn a desktop table page into a mobile card layout, and test portrait, landscape and safe areas on a real device.

risk-systems.name: Risk Control & Compliance
risk-systems.description: Tencent WeChat Pay builds a financial-grade risk control platform, Coinbase makes real-time risk decisions, Money Forward builds the AML/eKYC foundation, Reddit does compliance engineering, and Meituan identifies and handles trust and integrity risks.
concepts: Review, appeal and manual review flows
risk-systems.practice: Build a transaction risk control service with a rule engine, sliding-window features and a manual review queue, keeping P99 under 50ms.

rl.name: Agentic RL Infrastructure
rl.description: Training agents needs huge numbers of sandbox environments, rollouts and rewards. Both Baidu and Alibaba mention it.
rl.practice: Read an Agentic RL paper and draw its rollout infrastructure.

rollout.name: Model Onboarding
rollout.description: OpenAI Codex and Cursor both treat onboarding, evaluating and gradually rolling out new models as a core duty; Japanese JDs require version management and rollback.
rollout.practice: Simulate a model switch: run evals, canary to 5%, monitor metrics and roll back in one click.

safe-release.name: Change Management
safe-release.description: Most incidents are caused by changes. Feature flags, gradual rollouts, canary analysis and automatic rollback lower the risk of every release.
safe-release.practice: Configure canary releases for a service with Argo Rollouts and Prometheus analysis, then deliberately ship a bad version to verify automatic rollback.

sandbox.name: Code Execution Sandbox
sandbox.description: The environment where agents write and run code, and the core product of agent infrastructure.
sandbox.practice: Build a code execution service with an API on top of Firecracker or gVisor.

sched.name: Scheduling & Elasticity
sched.description: Scheduling, cold starts and scaling for huge numbers of agents and sandbox instances.
sched.practice: Design a warm pool for sandboxes and measure cold-start P50 and P99.

search-engine.name: Full-Text Search
search-engine.description: Tencent WeChat e-commerce roles ask for Elasticsearch, inverted indexes, tokenization and relevance ranking; Datadog uses Elasticsearch; PayPay's stack includes ELK.
search-engine.practice: Sync a product table to Elasticsearch via CDC, build a search API with filters and highlighting, and tune relevance.

security-basics.name: AppSec Basics (OWASP)
security-basics.description: Causes of and defenses against common web vulnerabilities: injection, XSS, CSRF, broken access control, leaked secrets and the dependency supply chain. Security has to be considered while writing the code.
security-basics.practice: Scan your own service with OWASP ZAP, fix the injection and broken access control issues it finds, and add dependency scanning to CI.

seo.name: SEO & Site Content
seo.description: Make sure search engines crawl and display pages correctly. Vercel lists technical SEO and CMS as a plus, and Ramp's growth role asks for SEO principles and a CMS (Sanity).
seo.practice: Add a sitemap, structured data and OG images to a Next.js site, and check indexing in Search Console.

service-mesh.name: Service Mesh & Governance
service-mesh.description: Use a sidecar or ambient mesh to handle service-to-service traffic management, mTLS and observability in one place, along with governance such as service registration and discovery.
concepts: Istio traffic management (routing, retries, circuit breaking)
service-mesh.practice: Install Istio in a cluster, set up 10% canary routing and fault injection for a service, and watch the Envoy metrics.

serving.name: Model Serving
serving.description: Understanding the inference side is what makes cost and latency optimization work.
serving.practice: Deploy vLLM locally and measure how batch size affects throughput and latency.

skills.name: Skills / CLI / SDK
skills.description: Product interfaces built for agents. Baidu calls this an Agent-Ready product experience.
skills.practice: Write a Skill for an internal workflow and observe when the agent loads it and when it misuses it.

slo.name: SLOs & Error Budgets
slo.description: Define reliability targets with user-centric SLIs and use error budgets to balance release velocity against stability. The core methodology of SRE.
slo.practice: Define 2 SLIs and matching SLOs for a service, implement multi-window burn-rate alerts in Prometheus, and write an error budget policy.

spark-batch.name: Spark Batch Processing
spark-batch.description: The de facto standard for large-scale offline computing. Airbnb, Chime, Tencent, Meituan and Alibaba all ask for Spark, often including internals and tuning.
spark-batch.practice: Process a public dataset of 10GB or more with Spark, deliberately create data skew, then fix it with salting or AQE and compare run times.

sql-db.name: SQL & Databases
sql-db.description: MySQL and PostgreSQL appear in almost every JD: you need to write complex SQL correctly and understand indexes, transactions and query plans.
concepts: Locks, deadlocks and slow query tuning
sql-db.practice: Reproduce a slow query on a million-row table, read EXPLAIN to design a composite index, then reproduce phantom reads under two isolation levels.

sql-transform.name: SQL Transformation (dbt)
sql-transform.description: Manage SQL models the engineering way: modularity, tests, docs and dependencies. Discord and Brex explicitly ask for dbt.
concepts: Models, ref and the dependency graph
sql-transform.practice: Use dbt to build a set of raw tables into two layers of models (staging, then mart), add uniqueness and not-null tests, and generate the docs site.

sre.name: SRE & Failure Drills
sre.description: Tencent has a dedicated SRE role for agent sandboxes that requires chaos engineering; Japanese JDs require fallbacks, alerting and runbooks.
sre.practice: Run a fault injection against your sandbox service and write the matching runbook.

ssr-next.name: SSR & Next.js
ssr-next.description: Server-side rendering, static generation and streaming. Vercel, Ramp and miive use Next.js, and Alibaba ATH asks for work on the BFF layer and server-side rendering.
concepts: Trade-offs among CSR, SSR, SSG and ISR
ssr-next.practice: Build a blog with ISR on the Next.js App Router and compare first paint and LCP with a CSR version.

state.name: State Model
state.description: Xiaohongshu (RED) specifically calls for research into state models such as Session, Event, Turn, Deployment and Workspace.
concepts: Event log as the source of truth
state.practice: Design an event schema for your agent that can fully rebuild state from the log.

stateful-ops.name: Stateful Middleware Ops
stateful-ops.description: Deploying, scaling, backing up and handling failures of databases, messaging, coordination services and distributed storage in production. Platform teams such as Cloudflare's run Postgres, Kafka and Ceph themselves.
stateful-ops.practice: Deploy a PostgreSQL cluster on K8s with an Operator, then drill primary failover and restoring from backup.

stream-processing.name: Stream Processing
stream-processing.description: Processing unbounded data streams: event time, windows, state and fault tolerance. Flink is the most common engine, with Kafka Streams and Spark Structured Streaming also widely used.
concepts: Event time, watermarks and out-of-order data
Checkpoints and the limits of exactly-once
stream-processing.practice: Read a click stream from Kafka with Flink, compute PV/UV in 5-minute tumbling windows, and verify that results are not duplicated after a job restart.

streaming-ui.name: Streaming UI
streaming-ui.description: Token-by-token output, reasoning and tool progress all have to render in real time. ByteDance Lark asks for SSE/WebSocket streaming rendering, Tencent Hunyuan for streaming output and poor-network handling, and Ramp builds real-time, agent-driven interfaces.
concepts: Displaying tool calls and task progress
Interrupts, retries and resuming after disconnects
Keeping frontend state in sync with stream events
streaming-ui.practice: Build a chat UI that streams Markdown and code blocks, supports stopping generation, and resumes from the last event after a disconnect.

structured-output.name: Structured Output
structured-output.description: Make models emit JSON that programs can consume. Ramp lists structured extraction as a core project (it open-sourced jsonformer), and Baidu asks for experience extracting parameters across multi-step tool calls.
concepts: Retry and repair on validation failure
structured-output.practice: Extract amount, date and vendor from 50 invoice texts, constrain the output with a schema, and measure per-field accuracy.

sys-design.name: System Design
sys-design.description: Making trade-offs among availability, consistency, latency and cost to design service architectures that scale. Also a standard part of most interviews.
sys-design.practice: In interview format, fully design a URL shortener and a news feed, including capacity estimates and three key trade-offs.

sys-troubleshoot.name: Production Troubleshooting
sys-troubleshoot.description: Narrow the scope layer by layer across application, kernel, network and dependencies, and find root causes by measuring rather than guessing. Almost every SRE JD lists it as a hard requirement.
concepts: Live tools such as strace, tcpdump and perf
sys-troubleshoot.practice: On a Linux machine under load, create CPU, memory, disk and network bottlenecks, and write a one-page troubleshooting log for each: which metrics you checked, which commands you ran, and how you confirmed the root cause.

tech-lead.name: Technical Leadership
tech-lead.description: Coinbase asks for writing design docs for complex systems and mentoring, Robinhood for leading large projects, Reddit for tech lead experience, and Meituan for solution design and review. This is what separates senior backend engineers.
concepts: Mentoring and teaching through code review
tech-lead.practice: Write a design doc for a real requirement (background, goals, options compared, risks, rollout plan) and take it through review.

tenant.name: Multi-Tenant Isolation
tenant.description: Baidu requires a high-security multi-tenant isolation design, and Alibaba requires multi-tenant isolation experience.
tenant.practice: Write a multi-tenancy threat model document for a sandbox platform.

testing.name: Automated Testing
testing.description: A layered strategy of unit, integration and end-to-end tests so changes can be merged with confidence.
testing.practice: Fill in unit, integration (a real DB via Testcontainers) and contract tests for an order service and wire them into CI.

toil-automation.name: Toil Reduction
toil-automation.description: Turn repetitive manual operations into code and self-healing systems. The SRE's job is to write software that solves operations problems, not to handle them by hand.
toil-automation.practice: Log your manual ops work for a week, turn the most time-consuming task into a tool or self-healing script, and measure the time saved.

tools.name: Tool Design
tools.description: Tools are the agent's API, and their design quality directly affects success rate.
tools.practice: Turn an existing REST API into an agent-friendly tool set and compare the two with evals.

trace.name: Tracing & Observability
trace.description: Agent execution paths are long and non-deterministic, so every step must be visible.
trace.practice: Instrument an agent with OpenTelemetry and view a complete trace in Grafana.

tracking.name: Event Tracking & Models
tracking.description: Designing the data source from client and server event tracking to event tables: event models, naming conventions, versioning and acceptance checks.
concepts: Events, properties and user / session models
Codeless / auto-tracking vs. client-side and server-side tracking
tracking.practice: Write an event tracking spec (10 events) for a chat product, and design the validation SQL used for acceptance.

traffic-edge.name: Edge & Load Balancing
traffic-edge.description: The full ingress path from DNS, CDN and WAF to L4/L7 load balancing, plus global traffic steering.
traffic-edge.practice: Draw the full path of a user request from DNS resolution to a pod, and mark the possible failures and troubleshooting commands at each hop.

ts.name: TypeScript
ts.description: The default language for frontend and Node services. Large projects need real type design, not just annotations.
ts.practice: Migrate a small JS project to strict TypeScript and write complete request/response types for its API layer.

virt.name: Virtualization & eBPF
virt.description: Anthropic's sandbox roles require KVM, QEMU and eBPF; OpenAI Codex and Cognition require virtualization and VM orchestration. A layer below containers.
concepts: eBPF for observability and network control
virt.practice: Boot a microVM with Firecracker, then use eBPF to count syscalls and network traffic inside the sandbox.

vue.name: Vue
vue.description: Still widely used in China and Japan. PayPay prefers VueJS, and Baidu Netdisk asks for deep knowledge of the Vue ecosystem and experience upgrading from Vue 2 to Vue 3.
vue.practice: Implement a minimal reactive/effect, then migrate a Vue 2 Options API component to the Composition API.

web-basics.name: Web & Browser Basics
web-basics.description: HTTP, URLs, the same-origin policy, the DOM and the event model: the foundation of all browser-side work.
concepts: Fetch, streaming reads and SSE / WebSocket
web-basics.practice: Write a page without a framework: fetch a cross-origin API, handle the CORS preflight, then explain each request header in the DevTools Network panel.

web-framework.name: Server-Side Frameworks
web-framework.description: Meituan asks for proficiency with Spring and MyBatis, and NetEase and PayPay for Spring Boot. The framework defines the request lifecycle, dependency management and data access.
concepts: ORMs and the data access layer
web-framework.practice: Build a CRUD service from scratch with Spring Boot (or Gin in Go), including auth middleware, an ORM and integration tests.

web-graphics.name: Canvas, WebGL & Wasm
web-graphics.description: Graphics, audio/video and high-performance computing. Alibaba Qwen's video editor asks for WebAssembly, canvas rendering and OpenGL, and Ramp lists 3D libraries as a plus.
web-graphics.practice: Build a canvas editor with zoom and drag on Canvas, compile a filter algorithm to WebAssembly, and compare the speed.

web-vitals.name: Load Performance & CWV
web-vitals.description: LCP, INP, CLS and resource loading. Amap asks for familiarity with Core Web Vitals and Lighthouse, and Notion wants to optimize page load.
concepts: Critical rendering path and resource priority
web-vitals.practice: Measure a site with Lighthouse and the web-vitals library, get LCP under 2.5s, and add a Lighthouse budget to CI.
